reviewAdvisory: The 8% current rate is not among the supplied figures and the draft itself admits it is unconfirmed, yet it is used to produce headline numbers (USD 8,100, 337.5%, USD 810,000) presented as fact.

Going from USD 2,400 to USD 10,500 is a 337.5% increase, not a 337.5% jump in liability as stated relative to the new figure; the draft elsewhere calls it a 337.5% jump while the correct framing is a 4.375x rise, and the number is derived from an invented base rate.
The USD 240,000 and USD 810,000 figures rest entirely on the unverified 8% assumption and are stated without the hedge used earlier in the same section.
The confidence section labels the 35% rate and date as confirmed while the same section concedes the current rate is unknown, and the body then presents an 8% baseline as if established.
These figures are unrelated to the Thailand excise tax and are imported only to pad the piece; the draft itself says they are unrelated, so they add no support.
A 1% move on USD 30,000 is USD 300, not USD 30,303, and the added excise at 35% would be about USD 105 only if the CIF rose by USD 300; the arithmetic as written is internally inconsistent.
